ai.literal: Experienced pain enduring, to living beings harm not doing, that nature indeed to penance form.
ai.translation: Enduring the pain that comes upon oneself and doing no harm to other living beings is the true form of penance.
ai.modern: தமக்கு வரும் துன்பங்களைப் பொறுத்துக்கொள்வதும், மற்ற உயிர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதும் ஆகிய அதுவே தவத்தின் வடிவமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core nature of penance. It consists of two main actions: enduring the suffering that naturally comes to oneself, and refraining from causing harm to any other living being. The word 'uru' means form or shape, indicating that these two qualities together constitute the very embodiment of ascetic practice. True penance is thus shown as both internal endurance and external non-violence.

ai.literal: Penance indeed happens to those who possess penance; those without that undertaking it (is vain).
ai.translation: Penance is fruitful only for those who already possess the inner discipline for it. It is futile for those without that nature to undertake it.
ai.modern: தவம் செய்யும் இயல்பு உடையவர்களுக்கே தவம் கைகூடும். அந்த இயல்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் தவத்தை மேற்கொள்வது வீணாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that the practice of asceticism or penance cannot be forced; it requires an inherent disposition. The phrase 'தவமும் தவமுடையார்க்கு ஆகும்' means that penance naturally succeeds only for those whose minds are already conditioned for it. The second half, 'அதனை அஃதிலார் மேற்கொள்வது' (those without it undertaking it), leaves the conclusion unstated but clearly implies that such an effort is useless. The word 'ஆகும்' (will happen or succeed) in the first half sets up this contrast, showing that outward acts of penance require an inward readiness.

ai.literal: To those who have renounced, provisions desiring, forgot-they I-wonder, other people, penance.
ai.translation: I wonder if other people have forgotten penance because they desire to provide for those who have renounced.
ai.modern: துறவிகளுக்கு உணவு முதலியவற்றை அளிக்க விரும்பித்தான் மற்றவர்கள் தவம் செய்வதை மறந்துவிட்டார்களோ?
ai.explanation: The couplet playfully wonders why everyone does not practice asceticism. It suggests that 'other people' (householders) have forgotten to do penance only because they are busy providing 'provisions' (துப்புரவு) to those who have already renounced the world. The particle 'கொல்' adds a tone of gentle wonder or rhetorical questioning. Thus, it highlights the necessary and complementary role of householders in supporting ascetics.

ai.literal: Foes destroying and friends uplifting, if wished, by penance will come.
ai.translation: The power to destroy foes and uplift friends will come through penance, if one so desires.
ai.modern: பகைவரை அழிப்பதும், நண்பர்களை உயர்த்துவதும் ஆகிய செயல்கள் ஒருவர் விரும்பினால் அவருடைய தவத்தின் வலிமையால் கைகூடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the immense power gained through asceticism (தவம்). If an ascetic wishes it, their penance grants them the ability to ruin their enemies (ஒன்னார்) and elevate those who love them (உவந்தார்). The word 'எண்ணின்' (if considered or wished) emphasizes that while ascetics possess this dual power, they only exercise it if they choose to. Thus, true penance yields ultimate control over both destructive and constructive forces.

ai.literal: Desired things, as desired, because of attaining, doing penance here will be attempted.
ai.translation: Because penance achieves whatever is desired exactly as desired, it is undertaken here in this world.
ai.modern: விரும்பியவற்றை விரும்பியபடியே அடைய முடிவதால், தவம் இந்த உலகத்திலேயே பலரால் முயன்று செய்யப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains why people undertake the difficult practice of penance. It states that penance has the power to grant whatever one desires, exactly in the way it is desired. Because of this ability to attain one's goals, the act of doing penance is actively attempted here in this world. The repetition of 'வேண்டிய' emphasizes the complete fulfillment of all wishes.

ai.translation: Those who perform penance are the ones doing their true duty. All others, caught in the snare of desire, do only vain things.
ai.modern: தவம் செய்பவர்களே தமக்குரிய உண்மையான கடமையைச் செய்பவர்கள் ஆவார்கள். தவம் செய்யாத மற்றவர்கள் ஆசையில் அகப்பட்டு வீணான செயல்களையே செய்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts those who practice asceticism with those who do not. The phrase 'tam karumam' refers to one's ultimate or true duty, which is fulfilled through penance. Those who do not undertake this discipline fall prey to worldly desires. Consequently, all their actions become empty and yield no lasting benefit.

ai.literal: As heated it shines gold like, will emit light pain as it burns, as it burns, to those who can endure.
ai.translation: Just as gold shines brighter the more it is heated in the fire, those who endure penance will shine brighter the more they are burned by pain.
ai.modern: நெருப்பில் சுடச்சுடப் பொன் மேலும் ஒளிர்வது போல, தவம் செய்பவர்களைத் துன்பம் வருத்த வருத்த அவர்கள் மேலும் தூய்மையாகி ஒளி வீசுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the process of penance to the refining of gold. Just as gold becomes purer and shines brighter the more it is heated in the fire, the character of those who undertake penance becomes more radiant the more they endure pain. The repetition of 'சுட' (to burn/heat) emphasizes the continuous and intense nature of both the refining fire and the hardships of penance. Through this endurance, their true inner light is revealed.

ai.literal: one's own life's self to cease him who attained, other enduring lives all will worship.
ai.translation: All other enduring lives will worship him who has attained the state where his own ego has ceased.
ai.modern: தன்னுடைய உயிரில் உள்ள 'நான்' என்னும் அகந்தை முழுமையாக அழியப் பெற்றவனை, உலகில் உள்ள மற்ற நிலைத்த உயிர்கள் அனைத்தும் வணங்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate reverence commanded by a true ascetic. The phrase 'தான் அற' (ego to be severed) is key, referring to the complete destruction of the sense of 'I' or self-conceit within one's own life ('தன் உயிர்'). When a person attains this egoless state through penance, all other enduring lives ('மன் உயிர் எல்லாம்') naturally bow down to and worship them.

ai.literal: Death even escaping will be achieved, of penance the power to those who have attained.
ai.translation: Even overcoming death will be possible for those who have attained the power of penance.
ai.modern: தவம் செய்வதால் வரும் வலிமையை அடைந்தவர்களுக்கு, மரணத்தை வெல்வதும் சாத்தியமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the ultimate strength gained through ascetic practice. The word 'nōṟṟal' refers to the endurance and discipline of penance, which grants a profound inner power ('āṟṟal'). For those who have fully attained this power, even the ultimate human limit of death ('kūṟṟam') can be leaped over or overcome. The phrase 'kaikūṭum' literally means joining the hands, signifying that such an extraordinary feat comes easily into their grasp.

ai.literal: The destitute are many, the reason being: those who do penance are few, many are those who do not do penance.
ai.translation: The reason there are so many destitute people is that those who practice penance are few, while those who do not are many.
ai.modern: உலகில் வறியவர்கள் பலராக இருப்பதற்குக் காரணம், தவம் செய்பவர்கள் சிலராகவும், தவம் செய்யாதவர்கள் பலராகவும் இருப்பதுதான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a direct link between the practice of penance and prosperity. It observes that the world is filled with people who lack what they need ('ilar'). The reason given for this widespread destitution is a simple imbalance: very few people undertake the discipline of penance ('nōṟpār'), while the vast majority avoid it ('nōlātavar'). The root word 'nōl' means to endure or practice austerities, suggesting that the rewards of life require a discipline that most people are unwilling to cultivate.
